messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-polish-medium-0108", "row_sha256": "dab4c438f00b1062311a142f58e18fa8faeb88f306af978814f081873677e641", "mode": "/polish", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Rewrite awkward phrasing into readable prose for the supplied profile, or plain prose when none is supplied. Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "the screen-reader audit for the new volunteer portal happened on tuesday, with two reviewers checking 12 pages and eight common tasks. one reviewer used NVDA with Chrome on Windows, and the other used VoiceOver with Safari on an iPhone. they kept notes separately and then compared where their findings matched.

most page titles were announced in a useful way, but two pages had headings that skipped from level one to level three. the skip link showed up on 11 of the 12 pages; on account settings, it moved focus to content below the first heading instead of to the main content area. form labels worked on the registration and sign-in screens, though the date-of-birth field was announced without its format hint. both reviewers could finish all eight tasks, but one needed the page instructions to locate the saved-items control.

the team recorded seven issues: two marked high impact, three medium, and two low. the audit covered the desktop and mobile layouts at the tested screen sizes, but not zoom above 200 percent, voice control, or pages behind the staff login. the current assessment is that the reviewed volunteer tasks were mostly possible with the two tested screen-reader setups, while the heading, focus, and date-format issues remain within the audited pages. this assessment applies only to those pages, layouts, devices, and tasks; it does not establish accessibility for the whole portal or for other assistive technologies.", "output": "The screen-reader audit of the new volunteer portal took place on Tuesday. Two reviewers checked 12 pages and eight common tasks. One reviewer used NVDA with Chrome on Windows, and the other used VoiceOver with Safari on an iPhone. They took notes separately, then compared findings.

Most page titles were announced clearly, but two pages had headings that skipped from level one to level three. The skip link appeared on 11 of the 12 pages. On account settings, it moved focus below the first heading rather than to the main content area. Form labels worked on the registration and sign-in screens, although the date-of-birth field was announced without its format hint. Both reviewers completed all eight tasks, but one needed the page instructions to locate the saved-items control.

The team recorded seven issues: two high-impact, three medium-impact, and two low-impact. The audit covered desktop and mobile layouts at the tested screen sizes, but not zoom above 200 percent, voice control, or pages behind the staff login. The current assessment is that the reviewed volunteer tasks were mostly possible with the two tested screen-reader setups, while the heading, focus, and date-format issues remain within the audited pages. This assessment applies only to those pages, layouts, devices, and tasks; it does not establish accessibility for the whole portal or for other assistive technologies."}]
